blocks.title: Predict: which ratio for a climb?
content: A plane climbs at $12^\circ$ at 450 mph. To find the time to gain 7 miles, which side is the hypotenuse?
answer: The distance flown: speed is along the flight path, so use $\sin12^\circ=7/d$.

blocks.title: Flight paths and bearings
content: Distance flown $=$ speed $\times$ time; altitude $=$ distance flown $\times\sin(\text{angle})$.
Bearing S $\theta$ W: start at south, turn $\theta$ toward west. North-south leg $=d\cos\theta$; east-west leg $=d\sin\theta$.
Way back after two perpendicular legs: distance by the Pythagorean theorem, angle by inverse tangent, then name both directions.

blocks.title: Model the skill: bearing components

blocks.title: You try: the way home

blocks.title: Check and diagnose: bearings and units
content: Report a bearing with both directions and the angle, such as S $26.6^\circ$ E.
Convert hours to minutes before rounding a flight time.
answer: The angle in a bearing is measured from north or south, so cosine gives the north-south leg.

blocks.title: Warm-up: sketch -135°
content: Sketch $\theta=-135^\circ$ in standard position. Name its quadrant and reference angle.
instructor_notes: Give 30 seconds alone, then a partner check. Ask which direction a negative angle turns.
answer: Clockwise $135^\circ$ ends in Quadrant III; reference angle $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$.

blocks.title: Reference-angle rules
content: The reference angle is the positive acute angle to the x-axis.
First add or subtract $360^\circ$ (or $2\pi$) to land in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$; then find the quadrant.

assets.alt: Four coordinate planes use equal scales and terminal angles 40, 140, 220, and 320 degrees. Each orange arc meets the x-axis and measures 40 degrees.
assets.caption: Every reference arc meets the x-axis.

blocks.title: Sketch, then find the reference angle
content: Sketch each angle in standard position and show its reference angle: $-135^\circ$, $1035^\circ$, $5\pi/3$.
instructor_notes: Draw the rotation in one color and the reference arc in another. For 1035 degrees, draw two full loops before the last 315 degrees.

blocks.title: Reference angles in degrees and radians
instructor_notes: Partners split degrees and radians, then explain each quadrant to each other before revealing.

blocks.title: Which functions are positive?
content: Quadrant I: all six are positive. Quadrant II: sine and cosecant.
Quadrant III: tangent and cotangent. Quadrant IV: cosine and secant.
Cosecant has the sign of sine, secant of cosine, cotangent of tangent.
Two sign clues: list the quadrants for each clue, then keep the one in both lists.
instructor_notes: Tie each sign to the coordinate: cosine follows x, sine follows y.

blocks.title: Two sign clues, one quadrant
content: $\cos\theta<0$ and $\csc\theta<0$
$\sin\theta<0$ and $\cot\theta>0$
$\cos\theta>0$ and $\tan\theta<0$
$\cos\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta>0$
$\tan\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta>0$
$\cos\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta<0$
answer: II or III, and III or IV: Quadrant III.
III or IV, and I or III: Quadrant III.
I or IV, and II or IV: Quadrant IV.
I or IV, and I or II: Quadrant I.
I or III, and I or II: Quadrant I.
I or IV, and III or IV: Quadrant IV.

blocks.title: Values from a point on the terminal side
content: Find $r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ first; $r$ is always positive.
$(6,5)$: find $\cos\theta$, $\sec\theta$, and $\cot\theta$.
$(-5,-2)$: find $\sin\theta$, $\sec\theta$, and $\tan\theta$.
answer: Check: $(-5,-2)$ is in Quadrant III, where only tangent and cotangent are positive.
instructor_notes: One partner finds the ratio, the other rationalizes and checks the sign against the quadrant.

blocks.title: Check the sign, the axis, and r
content: A student says the reference angle for $150^\circ$ is $60^\circ$.
Another writes $r=-\sqrt{29}$ for $(-5,-2)$.
answer: $60^\circ$ is measured to the y-axis; to the x-axis it is $30^\circ$.
$r$ is a distance, so $r=\sqrt{29}$; the signs come from $x$ and $y$.

blocks.title: Which ratio?
content: A plane climbs at $9^\circ$. You know its altitude gain and want the distance it flies. Which trig ratio links them?
answer: Sine: the altitude is opposite the climb angle, and the distance flown is the hypotenuse.

blocks.title: Climb, descent, and bearings
content: Speed is along the flight path, so distance flown $=$ speed $\times$ time is the hypotenuse.
Climb or descent: altitude $=$ distance flown $\times\sin(\text{angle})$. Convert hours to minutes with $\times60$.
A bearing such as S $38^\circ$ W starts at south and turns $38^\circ$ toward west (compass heading $218^\circ$).
Because the angle is measured from north or south, the north-south leg uses cosine and the east-west leg uses sine.

blocks.title: Time to climb
content: A plane climbs at $9^\circ$ at 360 mph along its flight path. How long does it take to gain 5 miles of altitude? Round to the nearest minute.
instructor_notes: Ask why tangent would give the ground distance instead of the distance flown.

blocks.title: Altitude lost on a descent
content: A plane descends at 260 mph at an angle of depression of $3^\circ$. How much altitude does it lose in 8 minutes? Round to the nearest tenth of a mile.

blocks.title: How far south and west?
content: A plane flies 280 knots on a bearing of S $38^\circ$ W for 1.8 hours. How many nautical miles south and west has it traveled?
instructor_notes: Sketch the compass first. The 38 degree angle sits at the south axis, so south is adjacent.

blocks.title: The way home
content: A plane flies north for 1.5 hours, then west for 0.75 hour, at 350 mph on both legs.
Find the direct distance back to the airport and the bearing the plane should fly.
answer: $\tan A=262.5/525$, so $A\approx26.6^\circ$. The airport is south and east of the plane: bearing S $26.6^\circ$ E.
instructor_notes: Require a sketch with both legs labeled before any calculation.

blocks.title: Bearing and time mistakes
content: A student answers the way-home bearing with $26.6^\circ$ only.
Another reports the climb time as 0.09.
answer: A bearing names both directions and the angle: S $26.6^\circ$ E.
0.0888 is in hours; multiply by 60 to report about 5 minutes.

blocks.title: Exit check
content: Find the reference angle for $-390^\circ$ and name its quadrant.
A plane flies 300 NM on a bearing of N $40^\circ$ E. How far north and east does it travel?
